# 2. A Guide for You {.unnumbered}

*How do I use this guide?*

This guide is your companion for the rest of the semester. Each week, you will
learn about a new mindset related to peer mentoring, review your score on that
mindset, and discuss how to answer the big question of the week. Each chapter
has the distribution for that week's measure and a **password lookup table**
where you can find your own score(s).

## How to find your scores {.unnumbered}

At the end of the anonymous survey you created a **password**. Each chapter
contains a table where you look up your password to find your composite scores
for that week's measure.

The tables show only the **last two letters and the four digits** of your
password. So if you created `BILLS8722`, look for **`LS8722`**. Dropping the
first three letters keeps the tables from identifying anyone, since passwords
often start with a name or initials.

The lookup tables are **grouped by stream**, and alphabetised within each
stream.

::: callout-note
## Save your password

Your password is the key to your individual scores all semester. Keep it in
your phone notes. To change it, contact the course instructor.
:::

## How to interpret your scores {.unnumbered}

Each measure produces a **composite score** from your responses to a set of
related items (usually their average; for the two point-budget measures, their
total).

1.  **Find your score** in the password lookup table.
2.  **Locate it** on the class distribution. The dashed lines mark the **33rd
    and 67th percentiles**, and the shaded bands show the **Low / Mid / High**
    thirds of the cohort.
3.  **Compare** where you fall relative to other FRI Semester 3 peer mentors.
4.  **Reflect** using the two prompts at the end of each chapter.

::: callout-note
## There are no right or wrong scores

These measures capture orientations and styles, not ability. The purpose is
self-awareness.
:::

## What is coming later {.unnumbered}

The survey you completed included the full **Mentoring Competency Assessment**
(Fleming et al., 2013) as a baseline. You will take it again at the end of the
semester, so unlike the other measures in this guide, that one is designed to
show **change over time** rather than a single snapshot. Chapter 4 uses your
baseline answers to place you in a mentoring-style quadrant.

The first mindset chapter, **4. Mentoring Style**, begins the weekly measures.
